headline: Fuel fake news crackdown: MCMC flags 96 posts, probes 17 under Section 233
context: On 1 April 2026 PM Anwar called spreading fake news during a global crisis an act of betrayal against the country. MCMC had detected 96 pieces of fake content; by 3 April it was investigating 17 people under Section 233.

changes.summary: Correction: Earlier editions said only 8 of 96 flagged posts were fabrications, but no source supports that: MCMC described all 96 as fake content, 8 was the number of people questioned by 3 April, and unsourced claims about past prime ministers and named parties are removed.

cards.big: The government is cracking down on fake news about fuel and electricity prices to protect Malaysians from misinformation.
cards.sub: MCMC had detected 96 pieces of fake content by 1 April. Two days later it was investigating 17 people and had statements from eight.

cards.big: The 17 face investigation under Section 233, which carries a fine of up to RM500,000, two years in jail, or both on conviction.
cards.sub: MCMC listed five cases over false fuel-hike posts and three over electricity tariffs. Nine more people were still being monitored.

cards.big: Anwar called creating and spreading fake news during a global crisis 'an act of betrayal against the country'.
cards.sub: He said the government had no choice but to order the police and MCMC to take firm action.

cards.big: MOF estimated petrol and diesel subsidies would reach RM4 billion a month. Public anxiety had a basis, and so did the fiscal alarm.
cards.sub: With crude above US$100 a barrel, MOF cut the monthly RM1.99 RON95 quota from 300 to 200 litres from April, calling the move temporary.

cards.big: On 3 April every case was still an investigation. The label 'false' came from the regulator, not from a court.
Fake price posts deserve investigation. When one post can draw a RM500,000 fine, MCMC should publish what it flagged and why.
